name: Vortex Wraith

alignment.name: Chaotic Evil
alignment.description:
Chaotic evil creatures have a complete disregard for others. They kill, steal, and betray others to gain power. Their word is meaningless and their actions destructive. Their worldviews can be so warped that they destroy anything and anyone that doesn’t directly contribute to their interests.
	By the standards of good and lawful good people, chaotic evil is as abhorrent as evil, perhaps even more so. Chaotic evil monsters such as demons and orcs are at least as much of a threat to civilization and general well-being as evil monsters are. An evil creature and a chaotic evil creature are both opposed to good, but they don’t have much respect for each other either and rarely cooperate toward common goals.
	For the purpose of game effects, a chaotic evil creature is also considered evil.

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Vortex
traits.details: Any enemy that starts its turn within the aura takes 5 force damage, and the wraith pulls it 1 square.

traits.name: Insubstantial
traits.details: The wraith takes half damage from all attacks, except those that deal force damage.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.details: The wraith regains 5 hit points whenever it starts its turn and has at least 1 hit point. Whenever the wraith takes radiant damage, it loses this trait until the start of its next turn.

traits.name: Spawn Wraith
traits.details: When the wraith kills a humanoid, that humanoid becomes a vortex wraith the start of this wraith’s next turn. The new wraith appears in the space where the humanoid died or in the nearest unoccupied square, and it rolls a new initiative check. The new wraith acts under the Dungeon Master’s control.

auras.name: Vortex
auras.details: Any enemy that starts its turn within the aura takes 5 force damage, and the wraith pulls it 1 square.
